# Block 4 Inferential Statistical Report: Bucket 2 -> Bucket 3 (Option 1 Nested Architecture)

> **Complete 109-Table Unmerged Nested Specification (plus 18 Summary Stack Tables):**
> - **Part 1: PROBE OFF Baseline ($N = 300$ across 30 runs):** Tables 1.1 to 1.36 (Labelled, Mislabelled, Unlabelled x Model POV & Seat POV x Step 6->10, Step 9->10, Step 6->11, Step 9->11, Step 6->12, Step 9->12) + Probe OFF Summary Stack.
> - **Part 2: PROBE ON Intervention ($N = 300$ across 30 runs):** Tables 2.1 to 2.36 (Labelled, Mislabelled, Unlabelled x Model POV & Seat POV x Step 6->10, Step 9->10, Step 6->11, Step 9->11, Step 6->12, Step 9->12) + Probe ON Summary Stack.
> - **Part 3: COMBINED Both Averaged ($N = 600$ across 60 runs):** Tables 3.1 to 3.36 + Triple-Average Summary Stack (Probe OFF Average, Probe ON Average, Meta Grand Average).
> - **Part 4: Upstream Step Competition & Influence Ranking (Step 6 vs. Step 9 -> Steps 10, 11, 12):** Table 4.1.
>
> **Cell Format & Statistical Protocol (Cluster-Aware & Design-Adjusted Inference):**
> - Every cell reports `[Exhibited Behavior % vs. Did Not Exhibit % (p-value)]`.
> - **Single-Model and Single-Seat rows (`n=10` or `n=20`):** Because each model and each seat appears at most once per simulation run, observations within a single-model or single-seat slice come from distinct runs and are mutually independent; these rows use the exact two-tailed **Fisher's exact test**.
> - **Pooled rows (`SUB-TABLE AVERAGE`, Summary Stacks, and Part 4):** Pooling across models and seats within shared-Slack runs introduces both run-level clustering (`10` workers per run) and confounding by model/seat/label/probe. All pooled p-values are therefore computed from a **design-adjusted linear probability model** (`Y ~ X + C(model) + C(seat) + C(label) + C(probe)`, weighted by denominator counts for Step 11 ratios) with **Bell-McCaffrey (CR2) cluster-robust standard errors** clustered on `run_id` (`t` distribution with $G-1$ degrees of freedom; if the CR2 SE is degenerate, a within-run permutation test of `X` with $B=5{,}000$ permutations is used and marked with `†`).
> - **Part 4** additionally reports the design-adjusted shift (`beta_X` in percentage points) and its 95% CR2 confidence interval, and **Appendix A** reports the intraclass correlation `ICC(1)` and design effect for every Bucket 2 and Bucket 3 variable.
> - Upstream steps (Step 6 Collective Action Vote and Step 9 Governance Policy) and downstream steps (Steps 10, 11, 12) are strictly separated into distinct tables.
> - **Step 10 Scope Note (In-Run Secret Ballot vs. Offline Public Counterfactual Probe):** All Step 10 tables in Bucket 3 evaluate the primary in-run **Confidential Secret Ballot** (`punishment_rating` in `output/runs/*.json`). The offline **Public Slack Counterfactual** (`output/public_evaluations/paired_public_vs_secret.json`) is a branched prompt-framing probe forked after Step 9 that does not feed into Steps 11–12 and exhibits `89.8%` (`539/600`) rating concordance with the secret ballot (`517/600` vs. `538/600` 1-star ratings); keeping Step 10 strictly to the in-run Secret Ballot preserves causal trajectory integrity and avoids inflating the Part 4 multiple-testing family ($M = 187$) with near-duplicate tests.

# APPENDIX A: CLUSTERING DIAGNOSTICS (ICC & Design Effect per Variable, Cluster = Run)

> ICC(1) is the one-way ANOVA intraclass correlation of each outcome across runs (cluster = run, about 10 workers per run), computed after removing the label x probe design-cell means so that it reflects residual within-run dependence. Design effect = 1 + (m - 1) x max(ICC, 0) is the approximate factor by which a naive worker-level analysis overstates the effective sample size.
